title: DISPATCH-able frame retention policy: 20 GB cap + hourly launchd cleanup
author: jill (operator directive 2026-09-19, post disk-fill crash: 'create a PRD that you can DISPATCH that will limit the farm surveillance Frames to 20 gigs, and make a recommendation on how often to run it or check And review the kanban skill before you do that')
plan_section: Frame retention policy. Today, infra/cleanup.py implements BOTH age-based eviction (FRAME_RETENTION_HOURS=24) AND disk-budget enforcement (FRAME_MAX_BYTES=10 GB), but NOTHING calls it -- not the daemon, no launchd plist, no CronJob. data/frames/ therefore grew unbounded: today it is 11+ GB across 7 cameras and 4 of those subdirs (OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR 7.7 GB, Front Door Outside 1.5 GB, OUTSIDE_FRONT_GARAGE 1.5 GB, OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR 1.3 GB, OUTSIDE_FRONT_POWER 981 MB) are nowhere near the existing 24-hour age limit because the cleanup module is dormant. PRD-V2-061 makes it run. Cap raised from 10 GB -> 20 GB per operator directive. Hourly launchd plist is the dispatch surface.
trigger: Operator 2026-09-19 (verbatim, telegram msg ~129099): 'Well, first I want you to create a PRD that you can DISPATCH that will limit the farm surveillance Frames to 20 gigs, and make a recommendation on how often to run it or check And review the kanban skill before you do that'. Previous operator directive 2026-09-19 (verbatim): 'Yeah, stay focused on the system drive that's still 450 gigs taken up by something' -- the system drive is 500 GB total; with the frame cap dormant, the data/frames dir alone consumed 11+ GB and was a meaningful slice of the 44 GB free space.
background: On 2026-09-19 the system disk reached 98% full (9.8 GB free) and crashed parts of the listener pipeline. After today's cleanup (HF cache 25 GB freed, worktrees 1 GB freed, frame-prune 8 GB freed) the disk is at 90% (44 GB free). Of the remaining consumed space, data/frames/ is the single largest growable surface under our control (the rest is Library / system volumes we cannot touch). infra/cleanup.py already implements the policy but no caller invokes it: grep shows only tests/test_cleanup.py imports it; the daemon does not; no launchd plist references it. This PRD (a) raises the cap to 20 GB (operator directive), (b) wires the existing run() into the daemon as a periodic call AND installs a launchd plist as a belt-and-suspenders fallback so the cap holds even if the daemon is down, (c) emits a Telegram alert if frames dir ever exceeds the cap, (d) adds a kill switch (operator can flip a single env var to disable) so the worker can be paused for forensics without uninstalling the plist.

operator_guarantees.git_maintained: Every story lands as a real commit on main BEFORE claiming done. Reviewer verifies via git log main --grep <story_id>. (Carry forward from V2-060.)
operator_guarantees.code_actually_written: Every AC is a re-runnable shell command with explicit expected output. No 'looks right' approval.
operator_guarantees.no_residue: After each story lands, the file MUST contain the new code AND no commented-out old code. No 'if cleanup_disabled:' branches keeping the old template. No backward-compat shims.
operator_guarantees.no_fallback_paths: No try/except wrappers that mask cleanup failures. No 'if frames_dir exceeds cap, just log' branches. When the cap is exceeded and Phase 2 (_evict_by_oldest) runs, it MUST run to completion -- partial eviction leaves the system in a worse state than no eviction. (Carry forward from V2-060 operator rule: 'None of the design leaves any fall back paths in place.')
operator_guarantees.tests_actually_pass: tests/test_cleanup.py must stay green. New tests cover: (a) cap enforcement with FRAME_MAX_BYTES=20 GB on a synthetic frames tree, (b) launchd plist XML validates, (c) kill-switch env var (FARMSURV_CLEANUP_DISABLED=1) is honored, (d) Telegram alert fires only when cap exceeded AFTER a cleanup pass, not on transient mid-cleanup overshoot.
operator_guarantees.daemon_untouched_except_wiring: Only one line is added to listener/daemon.py: the periodic cleanup call (every N minutes) and the daemon's KeepAlive behavior must not change. No behavior changes to motion_gate, vision_analyzer, telegram_formatter, or any other listener-side module.
operator_guarantees.plist_under_repo: The new plist file lands under repo (infra/launchd/com.farm.surveillance.v2-cleanup.plist) but installation requires operator action (launchctl load). Do NOT auto-load the plist; operator runs the load command after review. PRD ships the file, not the activation.

shipping_definition: (a) infra/cleanup.py FRAME_MAX_BYTES raised from 10 GB to 20 GB (single constant). (b) listener/daemon.py: every N minutes (default 60), call infra.cleanup.run() from a daemon thread (NOT from the RTSP callback thread). (c) infra/cleanup.py emits a Telegram alert to TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID via existing infra.telegram_alerts when frames_dir post-cleanup size exceeds 20 GB (a safety net -- means either the cap is wrong or cleanup is broken). (d) infra/launchd/com.farm.surveillance.v2-cleanup.plist committed with StartInterval=3600 (hourly) and FARMSURV_CLEANUP_DISABLED=0. (e) FARMSURV_CLEANUP_DISABLED env var (default 0): when 1, cleanup.run() returns immediately with {deleted_dirs: 0, freed_bytes: 0, errors: 0}. (f) Single commit per story on main with US-061x in the message. Working tree clean. (g) NO fallback paths in any file. (h) NO leftover TODO comments. (i) docs/cleanup-policy.md documents the policy, the run frequency, the kill switch, and how to interpret the Telegram alert.
scope_exclusions: Do NOT touch /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-refactor/. Frozen archive (read-only reference).
Do NOT touch /Users/jill/farm-surveillance/ (v1). OFF and stays OFF.
Do NOT git push to forgejo or GitHub. Operator reviews and pushes.
Do NOT restart the daemon. Operator restarts manually after merge.
Do NOT auto-launchctl-load the new plist. The plist file is committed; load is operator-direct.

Do NOT change FRAME_RETENTION_HOURS (24h) in this PRD. Age-based eviction stays as the first-pass defense; disk-budget is the second-pass. The operator asked about a 20 GB cap, not a retention change. If the operator wants to revisit age later, that's a separate PRD.
Do NOT touch alert JSONL retention (ALERT_RETENTION_DAYS in infra/paths.py) or audit log retention (AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS). This PRD is about data/frames/ only.
Do NOT add a second cleanup mechanism. infra.cleanup.run() is the single canonical cleanup path. Do not duplicate the disk-budget logic in the daemon or plist.
Do NOT bundle the Library/ system-disk audit into this PRD. That's a separate operator task (still in progress, awaiting operator to grant Full Disk Access or do the inspection manually).
Do NOT pre-emptively raise FRAME_MAX_BYTES beyond 20 GB. The 20 GB cap is operator-set; if 20 GB is too low and the system hits it repeatedly, that's a signal for a separate PRD with new sizing.
design_principles: Single canonical cleanup path. infra.cleanup.run() is the only function that removes files from data/frames/. Both the daemon thread AND the launchd plist call the SAME function. No duplication.

Two-phase eviction order: (Phase 1) delete empty directories, then age-based eviction past FRAME_RETENTION_HOURS=24h; (Phase 2) if total bytes still exceed 20 GB cap, evict oldest alert dirs until under cap. This order means age-based eviction handles 95% of cleanup work cheaply; the cap is the safety net.

Hourly run frequency. StartInterval=3600 (3600 seconds = 1 hour). This is the recommended frequency. Rationale: alerts that are <1 hour old are still in active viewing/audit window (Telegram delivery, operator review); alerts >1 hour old are increasingly likely candidates for eviction. Hourly balances 'don't waste I/O' against 'don't let disk fill up between checks'. The daemon thread runs at the same interval (default 60 minutes) so both surfaces agree. (Operator can override daemon interval via FARMSURV_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MIN env var, default 60.)
Cap = 20 GB. Operator directive. This is ~2x the current usage (11.5 GB today across 7 cameras) so the cap gives headroom for spike days without letting the dir drift toward system-disk exhaustion.

Telegram alert fires ONLY when post-cleanup frames_dir size exceeds 20 GB. This is the safety-net signal: 'the cap is wrong OR cleanup is broken OR frames_dir is growing faster than we can evict'. Without this alert, a misconfigured retention would silently fill the disk until the system crashes (which is exactly what happened on 2026-09-19).

Kill switch via FARMSURV_CLEANUP_DISABLED=1. When set, cleanup.run() returns immediately with empty stats. Lets the operator pause cleanup during forensics (e.g., examining a specific alert dir before it gets evicted). One env var, no code path branching in cleanup.py.

No fallback paths. If cleanup.run() raises, the daemon thread logs the exception, emits a Telegram alert ('cleanup FAILED: <error>'), and continues running -- the next tick retries. We do NOT swallow the exception silently. We do NOT default to 'skip cleanup on error'.

Plist is committed but not auto-loaded. The operator must launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.farm.surveillance.v2-cleanup.plist. This protects against accidental double-cleanup (daemon thread + launchd firing simultaneously). The plist runs as a backup: if the daemon is down, launchd still trims. If the daemon is up, both run but each is idempotent (running cleanup on a clean dir is a no-op).
Tests that exercise the OLD 10 GB cap are updated to 20 GB, not kept-and-skipped. (Carry forward from V2-060 operator rule: 'delete old tests not skip them'.)

recommended_run_frequency.rationale: Alerts <1 hour old are in active viewing/audit window (Telegram delivery, operator review); alerts >1 hour old are increasingly likely candidates for age-based eviction. Hourly balances 'don't waste I/O' against 'don't let disk fill up between checks'. The cap (20 GB) is the safety net for spike days, not the steady-state.
recommended_run_frequency.configurable_via: FARMSURV_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MIN env var (default 60). Lower values = more frequent cleanup at higher I/O cost. The launchd plist uses StartInterval=3600 (seconds) and is fixed at hourly unless the operator edits the plist.
recommended_run_frequency.tradeoffs: More frequent cleanup (e.g. every 15 minutes) catches disk fill faster but adds I/O on every tick. Less frequent (e.g. every 6 hours) means more disk headroom consumed between checks but less I/O. Hourly is the recommended default for a system where alerts arrive in bursts (e.g. dawn/dusk). If the operator observes that 20 GB is regularly hit between hourly checks, the right fix is to lower FARMSURV_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MIN, NOT to raise the cap (per docs/cleanup-policy.md).
